messages:
alex: Heads up — we're hitting compatibility failures when trying to rollout model v2.3 on the runtime pinned to 3.1. Staging CI shows KV cache mismatch and some tokenization diffs. Can we discuss unpinning the runtime for a canary in tonight's change window? @sre-oncall @marina
marina: Which SDKs are affected? I saw a client crash in the integration tests but not sure whether it's SDK or runtime.
yang: The short answer: runtime 3.1 doesn't include the new attention kernel the model expects. SDK 1.8 uses the new API surface so if users upgrade the SDK they'll hit runtime mismatches. We have two paths: 1) unpin runtime on staging/prod to allow 3.2+ (fast), or 2) backport a compatibility shim to 3.1 (slower, ~2h dev + QA).
alex: For customer-facing stability I propose: unpin runtime on staging tonight for canary (22:00-23:00 UTC), keep prod pinned to 3.1 until shim or full validation done. Canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% with abort thresholds. Thoughts?
deploy-bot: :gear: Change window created by @alex for 2026-03-20 22:00-23:00 UTC. Rollout plan: canary 1% at start, 10% after 10m if healthy, 50% after 30m, full at 60m. Approval requested from eng-sre and eng-runtime.
sre-oncall: Approved for staging canary only. We need automated aborts on error rate >0.5% or latency p95 +50ms. Also add a probe that checks KV cache hits.
marina: I'll update the rollout config. Adding health checks and a post-deploy smoke test. Snippet added to the rollout manifest: ```
rollout:
  strategy: gradual
  targets: [staging-canary]
  steps:
    - percent: 1
      wait: 600s
    - percent: 10
      wait: 1200s
  abort_conditions:
    - error_rate > 0.5%
    - p95_latency_increase > 50ms
post_deploy_smoke: curl -sS https://staging.api.redwood/test-chat | grep "ok" || exit 1
```
yang: Note: there's a memory allocation pattern change in the new kernel that only appears with long-context workloads (>10k tokens). Our staging tests didn't hit that. We should either include a synthetic long-context smoke test or keep initial canary traffic to short-context only.
alex: Good catch. Marina can you add the synthetic test? If it's risky we can limit canary to short-context customers and tag those requests.
marina: Added synthetic test in the smoke suite (long_context_smoke). Updated rollout: long_context flag = false for 1%, true only at 50% step.
deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary started at 2026-03-20T22:00:05Z — target 1% traffic to runtime 3.2 on staging-canary. Logs at https://deploys.redwood/internal/1765009123/canary
sre-oncall: Observability note at 22:05: latency p95 +12ms, error rate 0.12% — within thresholds. KV cache hit rate stable.
ops-bot: :info: tracing alert created #TR-4211 for monitoring the canary (auto-generated).
yang: After ~30m we observed a memory creep on a subset of requests that use extended context (>15k). It started low but trending. Reproduced locally with `python reproduce_long_ctx.py --model v2.3 --runtime 3.2`.
alex: Can we pause the rollout and roll back the canary? If it's a memory leak we should stop before it hits more traffic.
yang: I recommend immediate rollback of canary. Not safe to continue. We'll capture heap profiles and iterate on a patch.
deploy-bot: :warning: Canary rollback initiated by @yang at 2026-03-20T22:35:44Z. Rolling runtime back to pinned 3.1 for staging-canary.
sre-oncall: Post-rollback check: error rate dropped back to baseline, no increased CPU. Good. We'll keep monitoring for 1h.
marina: I've updated release notes draft and added compatibility notes: "Model v2.3 requires runtime >=3.2. Runtime 3.2 includes new attention kernel; workload with >10k tokens may be unstable until patch." Also created JIRA RED-9823 to track the patch and validation tests.
alex: Action items: 1) yang to root cause & fix (RED-9823), 2) marina to update SDK compatibility matrix and docs, 3) ops to keep prod pinned and communicate to customer success. I'll file a postmortem if needed.
yang: I'll attach heap profiles and a failing test to RED-9823 by EOD. Quick note: maybe we should add a runtime feature flag to gate the new kernel per-tenant. Would reduce blast radius.
marina: Agreed — adding feature-flag work to the ticket. Also posting a short note to #customer-success: "We paused canary for v2.3 due to long-context memory issue; no impact to prod customers."
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Prod runtime remains pinned to 3.1. No changes to production routing.
alex: Thanks everyone. We'll reschedule the canary once the runtime patch and longer-context tests are in place. :thumbsup:
